summary:
Rogue was too young to remember when her mama—her first mama—died. She thinks, sometimes, that she remembers bits and pieces; waiting for a warm kiss against her forehead that never came, the scratchiness of her crinolines and the pinching of shoes two sizes too small that only mama would have noticed as she sat in the church pew. Another woman—Aunt Carrie, her mother's sister—fussing over her, despairing over this half-feral child. She'd smelled of baby powder, Aunt Carrie, prim and proper and pinching; the smell still sets her teeth on edge. Daddy had sent Aunt Carrie away and spent the years following ranting about her meddling ways, until the line between memory and tale became too blended to see between. It's hazy, softened by time until it is only the occasional passing feeling of absence.
She can't escape Remy LeBeau. 5000 years in the past and half a world away and the pain won't fade a bit.
 
In the aftermath of an asteroid, Rogue must come to terms with the death of the man she loves, and the world that keeps on going in his absence.

How do you make someone fall in love? No, that’s not right. Love was never the problem. How do you make someone trust you after all you’ve done to make it damn clear they can’t? Jewels, money, really very dangerous alien technology, you name it—he could steal without a second thought. It was easy. A cake walk, really. But the trust and affection of another human being? This was different. This, Gambit didn’t know how to steal. And it was keeping him up at night like a man possessed.
She didn’t trust him, and he could hardly even blame her—no one ever did. But he was craving Anna-Marie’s affection like a terrible, irresistible addiction, and he needed to prove to her just how madly in love with her he was. He thought it would be easy.
It wasn’t. Not even close. There was something wrong with this woman—and him, too, but he didn’t want to think about that part.
He loved her. Madly. She wouldn’t believe him. And the more he tried, the more he was beginning to understand that Rogue’s heart had been broken a long, long time ago. Maybe it’s been broken from the start. He needed to make her believe that she could be loved at all.

summary:
「如果 Erik 是塊金屬，Charles 就是他的融點；如果 Erik 是個黑洞，Charles 就是唯一能存在的重力。」
在 1960 年那個神奇美好的年代，Erik Lehnsherr 曾短暫地以為自己擁有過陽光。他討厭 Charles Xavier，討厭他的財富、他的樂觀、他無禮闖入腦海的英國腔。
這是一段關於磁力與心靈、關於命運之手、以及那句從未訴諸於口的、只有四個英文字母（或六個德文字母）構成的告白。原著向心理自白，側寫 Erik Lehnsherr 那些關於「討厭」與「愛」的漫長博弈。
"If Erik were a piece of metal, Charles would be his melting point; if Erik were a black hole, Charles would be the only gravity that could exist within him."
In the magical, golden era of the 1960s, Erik Lehnsherr briefly believed he possessed the sunlight. He claimed to hate Charles Xavier—hated his wealth, his relentless optimism, and that posh British accent that intruded rudely into his mind.
This is a journey through magnetism and telepathy, through the hands of fate, and toward that unspoken confession—the one that requires only four letters in English, six in German, but a lifetime for a survivor to understand.
A canon-compliant character study focusing on Erik Lehnsherr’s internal monologue: the long, agonizing game between "hatred" and "love."

summary:
Vicki learned young that being different meant being unwanted.
Her father locked her away when she grew wings at thirteen. At seventeen, her voice turned deadly, and he threw her out for good. After that, she survived with nothing but an abandoned cabin, a Bible in her pack, and the belief that if she stayed small enough, she might make it.
Eight years later, Charles Xavier finds her. The X-Men don’t ask her to shrink. They ask her to stay. To belong. Through stubborn friendship, quiet faith, and learning to fight for people like her, Vicki begins to imagine a future she never believed she deserved.
And then there’s Logan. He sees the way she flinches, the way she apologizes for breathing, the way she tries to make herself invisible—and challenges all of it. Pushes. Calls her out. Stays anyway.
He should terrify her.Instead, she unsettles him.
Because Vicki meets darkness with quiet, stubborn hope—and she doesn’t leave people in it alone.
And Logan… isn’t used to that.
Extremely slow burn. Hurt/comfort. Found family. Two people learning they’re allowed to exist—and maybe even be loved.

He’s convinced they are soulmates, so he proposes a relationship to “save time”. One day before she turns 25, while he is already 28, they are waiting for her arm compass to point toward him.

Being submerged in a new way of living can be, figuratively, a very stressful time for a sixteen-year-old. New school. New city. New friends.
And a new family, which can be a very fragile subject to handle.
Especially when you are forced to pretend to be someone who is no longer alive; all while looking for your missing twin, learning to keep your uncontrolled powers a secret, and discovering how not to lose your own identity with a body that is very much not your own.
(Y/N) Maximoff did not sign up for family drama. (Y/N) Wayne did not sign up to die young.
Both of them seem to become Death’s favorite tragedy.
Can Maximoff not lose herself in a place designed to see her crash and burn at the stake? Will she be able to find a place to belong? Learn to own up to her situation and even get some peace for the girl who is no longer amongst the living? Get some proper answers in a city full of mystery and secrets?
Thankfully, most of the questions have a positive outcome.

title: Schön is Die Nacht
author: ErlyMisaki
summary:
Se arrodilla junto a la silla, seguro de que en algún momento las cosas van a caer por su propio peso, como siempre. Con cuidado, toma las piernas casi inertes, las levanta sin afán, y luego deja que el otro se cuelgue de su cuello con una confianza amable. ¿Confiaría alguien en su peor enemigo para llevarlo así? No cree. Hace palanca impulsandose con una se sus rodillas. Su otra mano se posiciona sobre esa cintura que siempre ha sido demasiado estrecha, en la que encaja perfecto. Quiere caminar, quiere hacer lo que se supone prometió hacer, pero el rostro que se esconde contra su cuello se lo impide. Es solo una respiración superficial, un roce del aire en su piel, pero se siente igual a desplazar toda su soledad a un lado. El cabello de Charles, largo una vez más, hace cosquillas también, huele a limpio. summary:
In the dust-choked frontier town of Sentinel’s Rest, law and lawlessness walk hand in hand. Jean Grey, dutiful daughter of the sheriff and promised to a man she does not truly love, has her life mapped out before her—corsets, church pews, and obedience. But when a daring bank heist throws her into the path of the infamous White Queen, everything she thought she knew begins to unravel.
Drawn to danger as much as she fears it, Jean finds herself torn between loyalty and longing, between the quiet safety of her father’s house and the wild promise of freedom beneath the stars. The White Queen, wounded and hiding behind lies, teases and tempts her way into Jean’s guarded world. What begins as a secret act of compassion soon threatens to bloom into something far riskier.
Beyond the fragile walls of the Grey household, forces stir. Gangs ride under moonlight, empires of greed cast their shadows across the prairie, and the railroad threatens to carve its way through the heart of the land. In Sentinel’s Rest, love and loyalty are dangerous luxuries—and every choice Jean makes may cost her the life she longs to live.

tags: No Use of Y/N for Reader-Insert
Reader thinks avoidance will solve her problems
summary:
The X-Mansion was a lot of things, but predictable was never one of them. When Remy LeBeau first arrived, the mansion’s atmosphere shifted under the weight of his charm. He’d entered the foyer with a swagger, the kind that carried charisma and confidence and screamed look at me. It was clear to anyone present that he was used to having eyes on him.
You glanced up from your place on the couch with mild curiosity. As interesting as lesson plans could be, newcomers were far more so, and you weren’t one to pass up the opportunity to people watch. You eyed him shrewdly.
He was tall, with unruly hair that fell into his eyes. His long coat swirled around his ankles as he walked, his measured footsteps made it seem as though he already belonged and that the mansion hallways had been waiting for his return. As if sensing your attention, he paused in his step, turning his head and dipping it smoothly.
“Bonjour, Cherie,” he crooned, eyes brightening with mischief. The drawl of his voice echoed through the empty foyer.

summary: Kurt Wagner has loved Logan for a very, very long time but still not as long as Logan has loved Jean. They're too little, too late. Yet despite the heavy burden Kurt has no wish to put them both in the position Logan is already in, a relationship of torment. Already they know how to quietly love a being who cannot so obviously return it. Now they will love him through his grief and loss, forsaking any hope of exposing this love for the gift of bringing comfort to a hurting friend.Logan is awash in his misery and grief at the loss of Jean when Kurt finds him in a bar far from civilization. It is the first time he realizes, while not mourning as he is, that Kurt is nursing a long-hidden pain and, despite what Scott might say, he's no idiot. Things slowly start clicking for the wayward man as he walks a path towards a love his broken heart isn't ready for just yet.

summary:
In 1999, Colette "Lottie" Manfred, a 26-year-old genetics PhD student, goes on spring break with six friends to a cabin in the Canadian wilderness. They're young, bright, idealistic, and a little carefree, and Lottie, who studies mutant genomes, just wants a week away from the sterile labs of Columbia University.
But the woods aren't empty.
Victor Creed has been hunting in these woods for weeks: wild, far removed from human society, surviving on instinct and blood. When he happens to catch Lottie's scent—floral shampoo, adrenaline, something uniquely human—something primal ignites within him. A need to claim. To possess. To destroy and protect in equal measure.
What begins as a massacre becomes a kidnapping, and then a strange and brutal bond.

No início, há estranheza. Depois, surge a curiosidade. Porque, pela primeira vez, não importa o quanto tente, Will não consegue entrar na mente dele. E o que começa como um simples desafio — provar que consegue — logo se transforma em algo mais complicado do que deveria.
Porque talvez não seja sobre conseguir. Talvez seja sobre esperar que ele deixe.

经过罗根和韦德自愈因子一天的努力，韦德的词汇水平终于提高了一点，虽然还不会骂人，也听不懂成人笑话，但比一开始什么都不知道的状态还是好了不少。
罗根从厨房里出来后，却发现韦德不在客厅。他循着气味钻进卫生间，看见韦德正对着镜子发呆。
“你怎么了？”罗根看着他有点滑稽的样子，好笑地问道。
韦德却难过地说：“我觉得我长得很丑。”
罗根脸上轻微的笑意慢慢蒸发了，他瞅着垂头丧气的韦德，一时语塞。
“为什么我长的和你们不一样呢？”韦德扭过头，无助地问道。
罗根的大脑还在呼呼转动，他几乎是人生第一次绞尽脑汁不想要让自己说的话伤到一个人的心。最后他缓缓说：“那是因为---”
---老天啊，他真的要说这个吗？金刚狼觉得自己的人设要完蛋了。
“……实际上你是迪士尼公主，这是你的恶毒后妈给你许下的诅咒，那就是你会比其他所有人都更值得被爱，但你会失去你原本的帅脸。”

O Governo Americano lhe impõe o dever de supervisor o seu próprio projeto social, que busca auxiliar a Integração de jovens visitantes, vindos do distante cosmo ou de outras dimensões, na frágil sociedade humana.

Wade had never considered himself an ‘open book’ type. As much as he was a walking chatterbox with no off button, he wasn’t the kind of guy who would overshare anything that mattered. There were many things he held close and firm to his chest, things that he couldn’t imagine anyone else knowing. Things that, if placed in the wrong person’s hands, could easily leave him heartbroken and alone. He knew damn well what that would feel like if he let his guard down.
Now, there was just one problem about this; that problem happened to be a comic-accurate five-foot-three-inches mini Hugh Jackman with steak knives between his knuckles that somehow, against God’s will, managed to read Wade like he was a collection of children’s nursery rhymes. But When a crisis across the universe suddenly calls our Bitter-Rogue forwards to aid a universe unlike her own, she meets face to face with a familiar face that pulls at the strings in her heart and turns her world upside down once more. However despite her past, she still agrees to lend a hand and aid her other worldly family within their darkest times.

Food as a Metaphor for Love
summary:
In the sterile silence of a Division 3 safe-house, a fragile calm settles after a storm. Reader, in a regressed but curious state, watches as the agent Lenny raids the depressingly utilitarian fridge. Confronted with "Poached North Atlantic Salmon Product" and a sad cucumber, Lenny demands inspiration.
Her question sparks a dormant fire. Reader’s hyperfixation reignites, and they slip into a lecturing tone, detailing the sacred tenets of sushi, like the necessity of shari, the precise knives, the reverence for texture and "mouthfeel." title: En la sangre
author: Sandrolas
summary:
Desde el otro lado del bosque el vampiro seguía mirando la iglesia. Media hora más tarde fue testigo de cómo las luces se apagaban. Su curiosidad por el cura sólo había aumentado tras establecer este último contacto. Su sed había sido acompañada del hambre por probar su cuerpo. Uno que ocultaba detrás de la sotana. Deseaba quitársela y hundirse en él. Se relamía sólo de recordar cómo su sangre había viajado hasta sus mejillas. La necesidad por ver cómo bajaría toda esa sangre por debajo del cinturón de su pantalón era fuerte. Tuvo que frenarse antes de volver a la iglesia y romper la puerta. Podría intentar amenazarle con dejarle entrar. Por lo que había escuchado desde los tejados de las casas de sus feligreses era querido y respetado. Un cura involucrado en su trabajo que seguro que entregaría su propio cuerpo para salvar a su congregación. Sería fácil, pero él no lo quería así. Lo quería suplicando por él como suplicaba por su Dios. Lo quería debajo de él, de rodillas, le quería suplicando por su tacto y por su polla.
La imagen mental de esos ojos azules mirándole desde abajo le hizo tomar su decisión. Sería paciente y cautivador, pero conseguiría tenerlo bajo él. Y entonces probaría su sangre.

title: i could follow you to the beginning (let's relive the start)
author: aftersome
summary:
Adeline remembered it without softness, because there was none: two years behind wire and concrete, time reduced to hunger and desperate survival. Hope had been something unspoken—and when light finally shone upon the dreary purgatory of the prison, it was not bravery that had moved them, but inevitability. They found each other once more against all odds, and only when the sounds of pursuit had faded did they stop to embrace, ravenous for the other’s touch. They’d wandered for weeks afterwards, beneath the cover of the forest, amongst the rustling of the leaves. Two ghosts learning to be human again.
And despite the storm of fury in her, the sight of this tattoo softened the sharp furrow of her brows—because for all Erik’s faults and for all their differences, hadn’t they, so many lifetimes ago, loved each other once?

title: A Walk in the Green Light
author: God_of_Springonions

Pre-Movie: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)
Crossover Between Fox’s X-Men And The MCU
Movie: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)
Kind Of Historical Fiction If You Squint
summary:
ARTEMIS JAY CONNOR has never lived without a war.
Even as a girl, only nineteen years old, when she dressed in her father's clothes to serve her country.
Everyone said the same thing: Communism was an evil that had to be stopped; these were the Cold War years. Dangerous times. If a great man like President Kennedy could be shot in broad daylight by a Red in Dallas, how could any American feel safe? Everyone agreed that communism couldn't be allowed to flourish in Asia, and Vietnam was the place to stop it.
Decades later, Artemis fought in the War on Terror as the new Captain America, until Steve Rogers came back onto the scene in 2012 and she passed the mantle back. She worked alongside S.H.I.E.L.D because she had nothing—no home, no family left—but her best friends 67' Chevy Impala that she treats as if he's coming back for it. It was Nick Fury who offered her purpose and a chance to exorcise her demons, and to be more than the empty ghost casing that could take a punch, and fight battles that others never could.

author: JackyJango
summary: Charles Xavier and Erik Lehnsherr were at an expo — a high-profile business event. Charles may not have been a familiar face in the steel industry, but Erik had heard about the young CEO of Xavier Pharmaceuticals. If nothing else, Erik can spot a bright mind when he sees one. The fact that Xavier was a pretty face on top of it had been a deal sweetener.One moment they were yelling at each other, slamming down the other’s view of politics, and the next, they were shagging like wild rabbits. Erik had thought that that had been it. But the next morning, he’d found Charles’s business card in the front pocket of his trousers, with a we didn’t get to finish our argument scribbled on it.Now, they meet a few times a week in a fancy hotel room booked under false aliases, like some illicit lovers. title: A Scarlet Scarf Shift

summary:
Charles chuckles and looks around. He pulls the scarf — that has begun to slide down — snug over his nose, leaving just his eyes open to the steady breeze.
He spots a sweet stall two shops to his right. The sweets kept on display are nothing like what they make in the mahal. He hasn’t even seen some of them.
Licking his lips, he walks closer to take a better look. He’s always had a sweet tooth.
There’s a man behind the rows of arranged sweets. He’s a year or two older than Charles’s twenty-one — at most — with a chiselled jaw and pale grey eyes. His hair shines a rich copper when it catches the sun. Charles gapes at him, scandalised, for the man is dressed in nothing but a red vest over purple pyjamas that sit over a thin waist. His tanned skin ripples over lean muscles and the breadth of his shoulders compresses when he leans over the wooden plank.
Realising that he’s been gaping, Charles clears his throat.

summary:
“D’ya,” you start, unsure if you even wanna get into this because the furthest you ever got with a philosophical conversation was when you asked him if he thought cereal was a soup and he answered food was food. So at least you know he doesn’t care for labels. You turn to lie on your side. You probably have a double-chin this way. “Do you ever think ‘bout what you’ll do? After all this is over?”
“After this?” He asks, cocking his head. But you get the feeling he knows what you’re talking about. He’s picked up on your discomfort. Gonna work off it. 
“Like,” you fumble for words and gesture to the room, the motel, the long stretch of road that waits for you in the morning. The lack of permanence to it all. Do you count in that equation too? “This. Y’know. The travellin’ and the motels and…ya ever thought about settlin’ down or somethin’?”
He grunts. “Why? You been thinkin’ ‘bout it?”
“Sometimes,” you mumble, almost as though you’re ashamed of wanting more than this, more than what he’s willing to give you.In the midst of October's gloom, you and Logan drive across the country—searching for love and running from it.

“No. You wanna fuss over me cause I got hurt, fine. But yer stayin’ home with me where I can fuss over you cause you been pushin’ yerself to the breakin’ point over what Bobby? I’m alive, I’m here-”
“And if I’d gone to sleep and you’d died and I’d just gone to work- what- how would I have known? Okay?” He can feel his skin getting warmer, hot in a way that he’s usually able to recognize as being dangerous. “I should have been there- I should- I should have been there. I should have been there and you died, Sam- you died and I wasn’t- I couldn’t even try to save you and-”
“And it weren’t your fault.” Sam whispers, though he’s holding him tightly, too tight- trying to ground him. “It wasn’t your fault and you don’t have to do nothin’ to make up for it. Is that why you been burnin’ the candle at both ends? Cause you weren’t there?”
Roberto just sobs, burying his face into Sam’s chest, crying harder when the scent of blood is stronger there, the bandages under Sam’s shirt hiding the wound.

Magda had been in love once.
Once, when she was young and wasn’t Mrs David Maximoff. She had fallen in love with a boy from the hills. His father worked at the Xavier Manor as a driver, and his mother was the head cook.
Erik Lehnsherr was his name, tall and lean-muscled. Erik couldn’t hear, speak, read, or write. But he had a fast brain and a quick wit. He had eyes of quicksilver that screamed troublemaker.
Sometimes, when her heart is heavy and the days are woeful, she wonders if her Erik will ever come into her life again.
When her Erik does come into her life again many years later, he doesn’t come alone. He comes along with Charles Xavier, the boy who had disappeared abruptly from the Xavier Manor after his mother remarried Kurt Marko.

title: Kiss Your Darlings

summary:
Charles stills. ‘What’s wrong?’ he asks, taking a step back and dropping his hands from Erik’s face.
Erik looks hesitant, brows furrowed and his flat lips pressed further into a thin line.
Erik is the most confident man Charles knows, be it in movement or thought. He’s straightforward and presses on without a sliver of doubt in his mind. This image of Erik, however, is unfitting — uncertain and unsure.
‘I’m not used to this,’ Erik says, staring at the thick oak door to his left as if contemplating flight.
This? Had Charles misread the situation? Had Erik not been interested in him during all those days spent together travelling across the country and finding mutants? He wouldn’t have pulled Erik into an empty room in the middle of training like a love-struck teenager otherwise.

title: Too Late

tags: Erik Lehnsherr Doesn't Know Peter Maximoff is His Child (X-Men Alternate Timeline Movies)
summary:
Peter slowed down time despite his inability to do anything.
He watched the fire slowly creep toward its target, millisecond by millisecond, hoping his dad would manage to block it before it reached him, hoping someone would jump in and absorb the hit, hoping for anyone to react in time before it was too late, but they couldn't. He knew they couldn't. The only person who could protect Erik right now was currently incapacitated, struggling against the sand that bound him. 
He cursed himself for how useless he was without his legs, at how little it took for Apocalypse to render him defeated. He would trade his speed for superstrength, telekinesis, time travel, anything that could free him and prevent what was about to happen. As he realized the futility of his struggle, all he could hope for was that the immortal decided to spare his father.
—

That night, Celia learned her voice wasn’t just voice anymore—it was a power she didn’t understand.Her mother didn’t take it well. Frightened and unwilling to face what her daughter might become. Hurt, confused, and desperate not to be a burden, Celia packed her bag, took her guitar, and left before dawn—telling herself it would make her mother's life easier.For the next decade, Celia became a wanderer. Taking the name Echo, she drifted across cities and states, never staying long enough to form roots. She lived out of van backseats, motels, and rooftops, performing in smoky bars and empty alleys.She was never trying to be a hero. Just a girl with too much power and too many memories, trying to do something good before she disappeared again.But no matter how far she ran, Echo couldn’t outrun the echo of her past—or the hope that, one day, someone might still be singing back.

author: Emberline
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
tags: Logan | Wolverine Being a Little Shit (X-Men)
summary:
In Regency England, Major Charles Xavier returns from war broken in body and shadowed by scandal. Society whispers that he is half-mad, that he married his friend’s widow too soon, that captivity left him unfit for company.
Newly created Earl Ferrars, Erik Lehnsherr - the first Jewish peer of the realm - steps into this world of glittering ballrooms and venomous gossip. An industrialist with his own scars and his own hunt, Erik is brilliant, uncompromising, and mistrusted as much for his bluntness as for his heritage. Determined to carve a place for himself in a society eager to see him fail, he has little patience for broken war heroes.
But when intrigue and treason draw Charles and Erik into reluctant alliance, admiration deepens into desire - and desire into dangerous entanglement. Together they must hold the line between loyalty and love, scandal and survival, ruin and the fragile peace of a kingdom still trembling from war.

summary:
John reached up and awkwardly adjusted the tie that he was reluctantly wearing as he looked around the room. It was filled with all sorts of important people that he figured he probably should know, and some of whom he actually did, but he might as well have been in that room alone for all anyone was interacting with him. Of course, there was the small fact that Charles Xavier was there. Charles was as lovely and charming as ever, and certainly someone better to speak to than he ever would be. Still, he was surprised when he realized someone was standing by his side, sipping at a glass of champagne. He turned, and at first, all he saw was blond hair, leading down to a sapphire blue suit that clung tightly to the man's very fit body. And then he turned his head, and John realized he was checking out Bobby Drake.

The room was dark save for a lamp on one of the nightstands. Sitting on the left side of the bed were Jean and Scott. Logan’s foot hit a creaky plank when he got to their doorway, and they both looked up at the same time. His body blocked most of the light from the hall, and the room suddenly seemed a lot smaller. He could hear their hearts beating in near unison. The room smelled like a blend of their scents, and for a brief moment, he wondered if heaven smelled like this. Like Scott and Jean and Jean and Scott.
Logan glanced around the empty hallway from the corners of his eyes and swallowed, stepping past the threshold and into their bedroom. Neither of the couple on the bed moved until Jean lifted her hand, eyes glowing blue as the door slammed shut and locked behind him.

Wade props his chin on his folded arms, cheek mashed against the pillow, staring at the wall like it’s the most profound artwork he’s ever seen. Really, he’s just trying to keep his voice soft, not push too hard, because he can feel Logan’s tension vibrating through the bed.
“Listen, pal,” Wade starts carefully, the kind of careful that sounds unnatural coming out of him, “if you ever wanted to try… like, really try, the way it’s supposed to go? With someone who actually gives a damn about you having a good time, not just—” he makes a vague little wave of his hand that Logan can’t see but still feels necessary, “—using you ‘cause hey, Wolverine’s a convenient cock-sleeve? Then, uh. You know. I’d be more than happy to show you.”
The silence stretches. Logan’s breath is hot against Wade’s skin, unmoving now, caught like he doesn’t know if he should back away or press in harder.
Wade keeps going, softer. “Doesn’t have to be today. Doesn’t have to be tomorrow. Hell, it doesn’t have to be ever. I’m just… sayin’. If you ever want that? I’ll make it good for you. I swear I’d make it—fuck, Logan, I’d make it perfect.”

For both The Odyssey and The X-Men
summary:
Erik has spent a decade from his home in Ithaca, fighting a war that was not his own and then against Gods and nature itself. Now, finally home, he realizes he has one more battle to fight before his husband Charles is free of harm and safe in his arms. Charles, meanwhile, has his own plans.
  Erik glanced up at the sky, a mottled grey with a few sparse clouds as meager decoration. The beach in front of him was barren. No people fishing on the shores, no birds or crabs darting to and from, only petrified branches and a few scattered shells. Still, Erik’s heart soared. This land, this beach left to ruin, was his home. Not as he left it, not as he wanted it, but it would be soon, once he saw Charles.

  Charles. His husband and partner in everything, left behind to rule Ithaca when Thomas Cassidy of Mycenae requested his aid. He hadn’t wanted to go. A war over a woman he never met, who left of seemingly her own free will, was of no interest to him.

  But Erik was not naive. A refusal would have meant he and Cassidy were on opposite sides. Ithaca could not afford a war right now. Not when he and Charles were transforming it into a sanctuary for mutants and intellectuals alike.

title: Introspective: Emma Frost
author: The_Anxious_Chords01
summary:
Emma Grace Frost has been called many things: a villain, a hero, an X-Man, a mutie, the most powerful telepath alive (which she’s not—she’s at least second, though she’ll only admit it to me), a headmistress, and gorgeous with a resting bitch face that could fracture glass.
 
  But most people just call her a stone-cold bitch.
 
  Hell, I called her that. Multiple times. Sometimes with good reason. Sometimes because I was trying not to admit that I wanted her to kiss me so badly I thought I’d combust.
 
  And here’s the thing. She is a bitch. She’ll own that. Proudly. But what people miss—what most people never even try to see—is that Emma Frost is so much more. She is soft. She is caring. She is gentle in the way that matters. She is my wife. She is a mother.

summary: John did one last check of things. The cash drawer was counted and locked, all the bottles were corked, and the dishwasher was humming on its last cycle. The only thing left now was to lock up. But instead of heading for the door, John’s eyes flicked to the far end of the bar.  He crouched, reached underneath, and pulled out a bottle of whiskey. Not for customers but something he’d bought months ago and tucked away for this day of all days.He pulled a clean tumbler from the rack and poured two fingers neat.  The sound of the liquid meeting glass was almost soft enough to be sacred. He lifted it halfway and stared at the golden swirl inside. “Happy fucking birthday,” he murmured.And then, just as the glass reached his lips, he heard it.  A cough–not loud, not exaggerated, not theatrical–someone’s real cough, coming from the hallway near the bathrooms.or: It's been five years since Bobby left John for Marie on his birthday of all days. summary: Failed scholar-official Charles Xavier is having a crisis of sincerity. When he failed on his path to have everything he was taught to want, he fell back to irony and wit to carve a life for himself. When he meets the overly-serious Erik Lehnsherr, a renowned and successful man that has everything Charles wishes he didn't want, how is it that he only sees himself reflected in those grey eyes?I despise autobiographical writing, and yet I can't seem to keep myself out of this one. So aside from a plot synopsis, and I'm really sorry there's barely any plot at all, I'll do my best to express the emotion that forced me against my will to write this fic below:The world is bizarre and terrible, and it's so easy to find ourselves becoming bizarre and unreal with it. But nature is real and sincere, and witless. And this awful feeling in my chest is real, too. So why is it that when I long for something real, like I'm starving, like that feeling when you haven't had a vegetable in ages and your body is just begging for something substantial, why is it that I still reach for my wit first, and scorn the New Sincerity?

summary:
Charles Xavier has spent the better part of a decade coughing up with marigolds. Seeing Erik again makes everything worse and better at the same time. 
  Erik wins. He smirks teasingly, his eyes glinting with that familiar spark from before Cuba. Charles wants to believe it. That this affection isn’t a tactic of some kind, or maybe Erik’s twisted way of saying thank you for rescuing him 9 years too late. It’s not real. Can’t be real.
 
  Not after the way Erik looked at him before. The coldness in his gaze as he listed off every mutant Charles allowed to die, the congealed disgust growing more and more with every word. The harshness - No, whatever love Erik had for him before Cuba was long dead. Charles knew that.
 
  He had known that for years, since the first marigold petal. He was just waiting for Erik to catch up. It shouldn’t be long now.

summary: Long, deft fingers brush the thick, gently humming glass, their path irreverent, clouded, lost. The too-bright technicolor of Charles’ eyes crinkle as he smiles just past Erik, blissfully unaware of the reality distortion that beams him into the cathode ray tubes of a pocket dimension, tucked outside of the grasp of time itself. summary: You lean forward to place two fingers against his forehead and your own and then your mind opens—you can see everything—His first kill (it's easy)His master's will made flesh (the bullet he is, the gun in his hand)The pain (pain like nothing he has known before, pain like being flayed alive)The memories of the cold tile of a lab, of blood in a sink, of screams (his or the screams of others? he doesn't know the difference any longer)"Well. That wasn't quite what I was looking for," you murmur, but your hand doesn't stop stroking his hair and the gentle rhythm of your movements soothes him enough that he can close his eyes. "Bucky," your voice sounds far away, like it's coming from a dream. "I'll be back in a while, okay?"The hand in his hair stills for a moment and when you bend your head to kiss his forehead the feel of your mouth against his skin makes his head feel heavy and he can't fight the desire to sleep, and when he wakes again he'll know the taste of your tongue against his, and the shape of your mouth.

summary:
And just like that, life goes on.
  
  Before he knows what's happening, spring explodes all around him, and he's been living in Wade's world for just over four months.
  
  He never liked spring in his other world. Just another year starting, another year he had to live through, just another year of guilt and self-hatred.
  
  But now, as he feels the weather getting less cold each day, as he sees the trees breaking out of their hibernation, it's as if the frozen layer over his heart starts to melt too, and slowly, very slowly, he allows himself to feel again, to laugh and get familiar with the thought of actually enjoying being alive for another year.
A story about how Logan learns to trust again— in people, in feelings and most of all in himself.

summary:
It's torturous. Like a knife grazing slowly on the skin. He needs it to sink in, deep, hard, he would take it good, bleeding deliciously. When he called out for Logan he thought it would be easy somehow, maybe it was Logan's soft face that time and that he just followed him home. He had this silly and stupid fantasy that Logan would ask him out or kiss him. And who can blame him? Despite his dirty mouth, he's a very romantic guy.
But it hasn't been easy at all. The day after, they were acting as strangers again, he doesn't know why. He could see the older man putting some distance between them.  It was over before it even really began. At least that was what he thought at first. But the thing is, he still can see it in Logan's eyes, the wanting, every time he looks at Wade he gets these dark piercing eyes, those are the same eyes he gave him there, on that dirty car, covered in Wade's blood.
So, maybe Logan is not interested in having a romance with him, but they sure could still enjoy it. So fuck buddies be it. Wade can do it, it doesn't matter if he keeps dreaming with holding hands and kissing slowly, he's a grown up man.
And as a grown up man he has decided to seduce the older man.

summary: You should’ve gotten the hint after the first date when the man barely strung together three full sentences between sips of his beer. The second one wasn't much better, though he at least grunted in what you hoped was appreciation at one of your jokes. And now, here you are on a third stupid fucking date, sitting across from him at a darkened dive bar, nursing a drink you don't even want while he sips whiskey in silence.You can't do this shit anymore. It's like the dryest edging you've ever received in your life, and you were over it two dates ago.“So,” you say, leaning in. “Do you even like me?”Logan looks at you, finally blinking after staring at you like he had forgotten you were there to begin with. You can almost hear the squeak of his grip tightening slightly around his glass. His brow furrows, but unremarkably, he says nothing.Dragging a hand down your face, you sigh, fed up. “See? There's the problem.”He grunts (big surprise), and he looks like he's about to say something, but then shakes his head and throws back the rest of his drink.Yeah. That’s what you thought.
